results.summary_before: This design generates a pulse-width modulated (PWM) waveform with a duty cycle set by a 7-bit input. An internal counter is compared against the duty cycle value to produce a high output while the counter is below the threshold. Testing requires a clock signal and an oscilloscope or logic analyzer to observe the output waveform. The design is a straightforward PWM generator with no external hardware beyond measurement equipment.

results.summary_before: This project implements a 4-bit Brent-Kung adder that takes two 4-bit inputs and a carry-in, producing a 5-bit sum output. The design is combinational and can be tested using a provided Verilog testbench with Icarus Verilog and GTKWave. No external hardware is required for operation. The project is notable for being a quick implementation of a parallel prefix adder, likely created in a short time frame.

results.summary_before: This project implements a custom arithmetic logic unit (ALU) that also supports neural-inspired operations in a separate NPU mode. It takes two 4-bit operands and a 4-bit opcode plus a mode bit to select from operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, bitwise logic, rotation, priority encoding, gray code conversion, majority, and various neural computations. The 8-bit output includes the result and error, sign, carry, and zero flags. The design is purely combinational and requires no external hardware.

results.summary_before: This SystemVerilog design performs grayscale conversion and Sobel edge detection on pixel data streamed in over SPI. A two-bit select input chooses bypass, grayscale, Sobel, or grayscale-plus-Sobel processing, and an enable pin gates the Sobel stage. An internal LFSR can generate test pixels instead of external data, and the processed result appears on a single output pin. The design needs an SPI-capable host such as a Raspberry Pi to feed pixels, and the documentation explains the pin mapping and processing modes.

results.summary_before: This is a factory test module hardened with LibreLane 3.0.0.dev38. It provides three modes: mirroring input pins to outputs, mirroring bidirectional pins to outputs, and outputting an 8-bit counter on both output and bidirectional pins. The mode is selected by rst_n and sel signals. It is used to verify the connectivity and functionality of all I/O pins on the ASIC.

results.summary_before: A VGA screensaver that displays a bouncing logo with an animated color gradient, similar to the classic DVD screensaver. It supports a tiling mode and solid color mode via input pins, and can optionally be controlled with a Gamepad Pmod. The design outputs VGA signals for a 640x480 display and requires a TinyVGA Pmod for connection to a monitor. It is a fun visual demo with minimal external hardware.
